title: The fitness tracker reveals a terrifying effect that alcohol has on the body during sleep: "Here are evidence if you were in any doubt …"
text:
The fascinating data of the high -tech sleep trackers show the terrifying impact that alcohol can have before bedtime.
The owners of the Oura rings, the sleeping jewels loved by celebrities such as Gwyneth Paltrow and Prince Harry, have taken the Reddit social networks forum to share the worrying impact of even a glass of wine.
A 60 -year -old woman wrote that she was “bewildered” by her sleep statistics “after a night in the city.”
“Seeing it for yourself comes home,” he said.
The Oura ring report showed that after a drunk night its resting heart rate, a measure of sleep quality with lower, typically healthier scores, with 15 percent increase to 52 beats per minute.
A higher resting heart rate suggests that the organ is having to work harder, and studies have found that consistently high reading can be a sign of a higher risk of cardiovascular disease and death.
Similarly, its heart rate variability (HRV), a measure of the time range between heartbeat, with higher scores typically better, also received a blow.
She said the 18 millisecond HRV recorded by the ring was half of her usual reading of ‘The High 30s’.
Fascinating statistics collected from high -tech rings have revealed how bad drink alcohol can alter their dream
The Oura ring, launched in 2013 by Oura Health, a Finnish technology company, comes with a high price, from £ 299 and which costs until £ 549
A user, a 60 -year -old woman, said she was ‘baffled by my sleep statistics after one night in the city’
She wrote that she believes that her HRV fall was a sign that alcohol had put stress in her body, causing her heart to work harder than usual.
When commenting on the results earlier this week, he said that the data would make it think twice before going back some vessels again.
“I am not a great drinker, the last time I had alcohol before last night was the end of November,” he wrote.
‘But these statistics, however, will make me stop the next time I think about having a drink. At least, I would be thinking of limiting it to one or two.
Another Oura user shared how to have only one glass of wine, a night ritual for many British, had destroyed his dream.
They said that having the equivalent of just over 1.5 alcohol units had led to a horrible night of sleep and a depression at Oura scores.
The user reported an increase in heart rate, a leap to what he described as an unusually high 59 beats per minute.
Another Oura user shared how to have only one glass of wine, a night ritual for many British, had destroyed his dream
Prince Harry made a buzz around the Oura ring in 2018 when he was broken with titanium jewels during a trip to Australia. He took the black band on his right ring finger in the first three days of exits in Australia with his wife Meghan Markle
Responding to the publication, another user said he had a very similar experience with a glass of wine.
‘My resting heart rate is +10. It is good to know that the ring is really monitoring things.
A normal resting rate is between 60 and 100 beats per minute when it is awake, although this generally falls to 50 to 50 beats per minute while sleeping.
Research has linked a greater heart rate at rest with a higher risk of premature death. A study in 2013 found that men with a heart rate over 90 had triple the risk of premature death.
Normal HRV, on the other hand, varies significantly by age and individual.
Dr. Jabeen Begum told him Webmd The average HRV for a healthy adult is 42 milliseconds, although it can vary from between 19 and 75 milliseconds.
Oura said he has seen the impact of alcohol on sleep data shared by users on a larger scale.
In a report, the company said that alcohol consumption led to an average increase of five percent in resting heart rate compared to the typical average of a user.
Similarly, they found that HRV decreased by an average of 12 percent after drinking and the amount of ‘deep sleep’ rejuvenating fell on an average of 7 percent.
The Oura ring was launched in 2013 and C Oms with a considerable price, starting at £ 299 and costs until £ 549 for some versions.
Wellness Guru Gwyneth Paltrow, 52, has shared photos of herself with the ring on multiple occasions
Within the ring there are three sensors: small infrared lights that measure the heart and the frequency of breathing, an accelerometer to track the movement and a body temperature monitor that sees fevers and monitors the menstrual cycles of women.
Unlike many similar trackers, which often come in shape and function of watches, Oura says that its ring design distinguishes it.
The location, with the recommended index finger, means that captures signals directly from the heart to provide more precise data than those collected from devices used by the wrist.
Last year, scientists discovered that Oura data could be used to help predict whether a user had diabetes, flu or covid.
Adults are recommended to arrive between seven and nine hours of sleep per night.
However, the surveys suggest that the average British obtains only six hours and 20 minutes per night.
